xstage_coalesce: assigned x staging path (reader row-major stick read + fused tilize twin). Beginning required reading.

Read op_design.md (secs 1-6), changelog.md (all refinements), reader.cpp (reader_xstage block ~line 311), compute.cpp (compute_tilize block ~line 176). Confirmed baseline: 32 separate noc_async_read calls of kr*64B (1472B at kr=23) per stick, then self-copy L1->L1 via cb_x_stage, tilize<KR_PAD,cb_x_in,cb_x_stage>(1,32) asymmetric page mode.

Read compute.cpp, reader.cpp, writer.cpp in full. Confirmed: gate/up matmul is 1 in1-subblock call (GU_IN1_SUBBLOCKS=HN_PAD/HN_BLOCK, currently=1), then reduce loop over num_children with whole-block add. Reduce transport = child: copy acc->send CB, wait parent invite (SEM_GO), unicast write to parent slot + inc SEM_DATA; parent: invite (SEM_GO inc), wait SEM_DATA, add in-place. REDUCE_SLOTS=1 today (sequential waves). Now reading program_descriptor.py for HN_BLOCK/OUT_SUBBLOCK_H_GU comments and the reduce tree host-side construction.

Traced ckernel::matmul_block -> _llk_unpack_AB_matmul_ (tt_llk_blackhole). reuse_a = (ct_dim>=rt_dim); with our shape rt_dim=out_subblock_h=1, ct_dim=out_subblock_w=6 so reuse_a=true: in0 (SrcB) unpacked ONCE per call via single TTI_UNPACR, then hardware MOP loops ct_dim times unpacking a NEW in1 tile into SrcA each iter (in0 already amortized over out_subblock_w=6 WITHIN one call). The redundancy is ACROSS the 2 separate matmul_block HELPER calls (gate, up): each call re-unpacks the same in0 K-tiles independently. Also confirmed in matmul_block_helpers.inl: in0_index resets to in0_index_subblock_offset at the START of EACH in1_subblock iteration (nested inside in1_subblock loop) -> merging gate+up into ONE helper call with in1_num_subblocks=2 does NOT share in0 unpack either (same re-walk pattern) -- this is a predictable NULL for option 2, to be confirmed by measurement. True cross-matrix in0 sharing would require raw LLK skipping the SrcB reunpack between two separate tile_regs_acquire cycles (risk: srcreg-bank dvalid handshake, tt-llk has a dedicated srcreg-bank-sync-audit skill for exactly this hazard class) -- flagged as high risk/BLOCKED-candidate for hand-rolling on a shared device. Plan: build safe variants (baseline 2-call, merged-subblock 1-call in1_num_subblocks=2, out_subblock_w sweep, SKIP_COMPUTE ablation for unpack-bound confirmation) as the isolated bench; attempt raw LLK only if time/risk budget allows.

Scaled-down but faithful microbenchmark plan: 6 cores (not 110), depth-2 tree (root + 4 children, one child has its own child) to keep tractable while preserving asymmetric-depth serialization. Each core has its own K-slice of x/w_gate/w_up (kr=23,HN_PAD=6 tiles matching focus shape), no mcast needed since Kg is not reuse-shared within a column. Reading matmul_block_helpers.hpp next for in0 addressing to support M-axis sub-block splitting.

Confirmed repo-root conftest.py (tt-metal/conftest.py:427) defines the device fixture and applies repo-wide, so the pytest test file can live inside perf_experiments/gateup_in0_share/ (staying strictly in my dir) without losing fixture access. All under compute_kernel_config() matching real op default_compute_kernel_config() (LoFi, approx, fp32_dest_acc_en=False, dst_full_sync_en=False, bfp8_pack_precise=True) -- precision contract fixed identically across variants. Next: write the pytest test file (correctness PCC gate + device-ns measurement + predicate sweep) in the same dir.

Wrote isolated bench: gateup_in0_share.py (3 kernel variants: baseline 2-call, merged_1call 1-call w/ in1_num_subblocks=2 over concatenated W_gate|W_up, wide_subblock out_subblock_w sweep) + test_gateup_in0_share.py (single test function: correctness PCC checks, predicate sweep over kr in {23,22,20,19}, m_eff in {8,4,1}, ragged hn_real=4 baseline-only, SKIP_COMPUTE ablation, wide_subblock sweep w in {2,3,4,6,8} at N=24). Module loaded via importlib file-path (no __init__.py added to shared perf_experiments/ parent, avoiding collision with sibling root_epilogue_fusion dir). About to run scripts/run_safe_pytest.sh on it -- first device run, expect possible compile errors to fix.

Finalized microbench design: 10-core column (0,0)-(0,9) reproducing EXACT real reduce-tree topology for KGROUPS=10 (root row0, children 1,2,4,8; row4 has 2 children 5,6; row6 has child 7; row2 has child3; row8 has child9). No mcast needed (Kg not reuse-shared within a column). Each stage S needs compile-time CB ids for add<>/copy<>/mul<> eltwise_convenience helpers (InputSpec/OutputSpec are non-type template params), so compute.cpp uses a templated StageRunner<STAGE,S,PIPELINED> recursion to unroll stages at compile time, letting PIPELINED variant issue matmul(stage+1) BEFORE reduce-wait(stage) in program order. HN-split shares x across stages (1 CB, popped on last stage); weight per-stage (S CBs). M-split inverse. CB budget: reused gate_silu/gate_send as one shared per-stage CB pair (root vs non-root mutually exclusive use) to stay under 64 CB limit. Starting to write kernels now.

Read eltwise_chain.hpp/.inl + accumulation.cpp/dest_reuse_param.cpp/fused_chain.cpp kernel_lib tests. Found examples/eltwise_l1_vs_dest_accumulate.py and compute_fusion use a STALE pre-refactor API (InputLifecycle/OutputLifecycle no longer exist) - built my kernel against the CURRENT eltwise_chain API instead (input()/output(), WaitPolicy/PopPolicy/ReservePolicy/PushPolicy, L1Accumulation, DestReuseBinary). Key finding: eltwise_chain L1Accumulation OutputSpec pins pack address (many:1 reduce) so it cannot do position-preserving multi-tile accumulate; switched pack_l1_acc variant to raw pack_reconfig_l1_acc(1)/(0) toggle around a position-advancing copy<>, matching the real ops own down-matmul mechanism and the prompts own suggested fallback. dest_acc variant uses DestReuseBinary chain elements (documented, non-raw) to sum seed+fan_in children in a sticky bf16 DEST window per 8-tile block. Wrote bench.py (kernel + program descriptor + option-5 fuse variant) in my experiment dir.

Built isolated micro-bench under perf_experiments/xstage_coalesce/: xstage_reader.cpp/xstage_compute.cpp/xstage_writer.cpp (VARIANT 0=baseline,1=wide_read_individual,2=bank_run_grouped,3=dual_noc_split,4=bfp8_tile_direct,5=self_copy_ablation) + rateprobe_reader.cpp (raw transaction-count sweep) + test_xstage_bench.py (program descriptors, correctness vs ttnn tilize reference + bit-exact cross-variant check, perf via DEVICE KERNEL DURATION one-shot measurement). About to smoke-test variant 0 correctness on device.

Discovered add<>/mul<> convenience wrappers default to WaitPolicy::PerTile/PopPolicy::PerTile inputs, which eltwise_chain clamps block_size to 1 for (chain_supports_block_v requires Upfront/Cumulative/PerChunk). So production up-add and swiglu-mul each run 48 separate 1-tile DEST windows, not 1 window of 48. Real baseline = 8(bias)+48(up-add)+48(mul)=104 DEST windows. Designed 5-variant menu: baseline, blocked_3pass (fix block size only), hoisted_bias (+hoist reconfig/init), fused_up_mul (fuse up-add+mul via binary_dest_reuse_tiles DEST-reuse, no up_sum CB), fused_math_silu (same but SiLU on MATH thread via raw silu_tile, prices loss of packer-thread overlap). DEST accounting: HN_PAD=6 tiles already uses 6/8 DEST slots for one operand, so a true single-window 4-op fuse (needs 12) is infeasible without narrowing HN_BLOCK (out of scope, shared infra). Wrote program_descriptor_with_inline_kernels.py using raw LLK (add_tiles/add_tiles_init/binary_dest_reuse_tiles(_init)/silu_tile/pack_tile) for candidates 1-4, real kernel_lib helpers for baseline. Single-core sharded-L1 bench, tensor-backed CBs via cb_descriptor_from_sharded_tensor, mirroring examples/compute_block_size and examples/compute_fusion patterns.

pytest --import-mode=importlib cannot collect a test_*.py file placed directly inside ttnn/ttnn/operations/... : it derives a dotted module path starting with ttnn, inserts the repo-level parent onto sys.path, and re-executes ttnn/ttnn/__init__.py under a second qualified name (ttnn.ttnn), which crashes on duplicate C++ op registration (bernoulli). Confirmed this is why every real test in the repo lives under tests/, never inside ttnn/ttnn/. FIX: keep all program-descriptor/library logic as a plain (non-collected) module inside my experiment dir (xstage_bench.py), add a thin, uniquely-named pytest entry file under tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/moe_fused_swiglu/perf_probes/test_xstage_coalesce_bench.py that imports it. No real-op files touched.

Bake-off test PASSED (all correctness pcc~0.9999). KEY RESULT: merged_1call (single matmul_block call, in1_num_subblocks=2, concatenated W_gate|W_up) is WITHIN NOISE of baseline (2 separate calls) across the ENTIRE predicate sweep (kr in 23/22/20/19, m_eff in 8/4/1) -- speedup 1.001x-1.006x everywhere. This EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMS the matmul_block_helpers.inl code-reading prediction: in0_index resets to the subblock offset at the top of EVERY in1_subblock iteration, so in0 is NOT shared/reused across in1 sub-blocks -- a real, useful NULL for the core idea. SKIP_COMPUTE ablation at focus shape: 2932.9ns (skip) vs 28559.1ns (full) -> unpack+math = 89.7% of the compute_gateup stage in isolation (L1-resident) -- confirms unpack-bound stage, consistent with design docs 19-35us unpack roofline claim (measured clean number 28.6us sits in that band, below the real op min 34.6us, consistent with DRAM-wait removed). wide_subblock sweep (out_subblock_w 2->8, same total FMA, bfp8/bfp4): only 1.000x->1.032x (3.2% max) -- MUCH smaller than the bf16/bf16 1.46x cited for matmul_output_subblock, because bfp8/bfp4 unpack bytes are already small vs fixed per-call overhead. Computed theoretical ceiling for a hypothetical raw-LLK in0-share (eliminating the redundant 2nd in0 unpack): in0 is 1088B of 4544B unpack bytes per 6-FMA call (24%), so sharing removes ~12% of TOTAL unpack bytes across both matrices -> ~6% of the isolated compute_gateup window, i.e. only 1-2 percentage points of the WHOLE op given DRAM coupling. Given that bound is small and raw LLK SrcA/SrcB dvalid-bank sharing across two tile_regs cycles is a known hazard class (tt-llk srcreg-bank-sync-audit exists specifically for this), decided NOT to attempt raw LLK on the shared device -- reported as an analyzed-not-built option with its bound, matching the ops own Lever-4 precedent (analysed, deliberately not built). VERDICT: NULL for the assigned in0-sharing idea; a small separable wide-subblock lever exists but is not actionable here since HN_PAD=6 is grid-pinned (ceil(64/11)), not a free knob. Artifact: ttnn/ttnn/operations/moe_fused_swiglu/perf_experiments/gateup_in0_share/ (gateup_in0_share.py, test_gateup_in0_share.py, __init__.py). Test PASSED, left on disk uncommitted.

Wrote kernels/gru_compute.cpp, kernels/gru_reader.cpp, kernels/gru_writer.cpp, gru_program_descriptor.py, test_gru_bakeoff.py under perf_experiments/gateup_reduce_overlap/. About to run a single baseline correctness case first (S=1) with --dev to catch compile/hang issues before the full sweep.

static_assert(PAGES_PER_BANK>0,...) inside if-constexpr(VARIANT==2) fired for ALL variants (kernel_main is non-templated so the discarded-statement exemption for static_assert does not apply outside templates). Removed the compile-time assert; the host-side python assert already covers NUM_BANKS dividing TILE_H. Retrying build.

All 5 variants (0-4) pass PCC>=0.999 vs ttnn tilize reference; nonzero-kstart addressing check passes; variants 1,2,3 (wide_read,bank_run,dual_split) are BIT-IDENTICAL to variant 0 baseline. Moving to perf measurement: focus shape first.

First device run hung. Triage (captured synchronously from run_safe_pytest stdout, trustworthy) shows core (0,0) trisc0(UNPACK) stuck inside add_tiles->_llk_unpack_AB_->wait_for_next_context->semaphore_read, called directly from chlkc_unpack.cpp (matches add_bias_bcast_rows internal raw add_tiles call, stage (a) of baseline). trisc1(MATH)/trisc2(PACK) on the SAME core both sitting at trisc.cc:135 (the outer while(*trisc_run!=GO) dispatch-wait loop) -- i.e. never entered kernel_main for this launch. Suspect a dispatch-level or hw_startup/CB-setup issue in my minimal single-compute-kernel program (no reader/writer). Also note: a second, unrelated-looking triage dump read moments later via bare cat (CB ids 2,3,2) is likely a SIBLING subagents shared triage.txt path race, not mine -- disregarding it. Debugging via tt-probe --dev with DEVICE_PRINT next.

Focus shape (emb=7168,KR_PAD=23) single-core isolated (no 110-core contention): baseline=3490ns, wide_read_individual=8659ns (2.5x REGRESSION), bank_run_grouped=8736ns (2.5x REGRESSION), dual_noc_split=3010ns (-13.7% WIN), bfp8_tile_direct=1867ns (46% less -- bounds RM/tilize overhead), self_copy_ablation=3056ns (self-copy costs ~434ns=12%). Key honest caveat: isolated single-core numbers are far below the real ops multi-core-contention 15-40us range, so absolute deltas wont transfer 1:1, but the ranking (wide/bank_run lose, dual_split wins modestly) should hold or worsen for the loser variants under contention since they move strictly more DRAM bytes. Proceeding to rate probe + predicate sweep.

Collection failed with RuntimeError: Operation bernoulli already registered / ttnn.ttnn double-import, reproducible 100% via plain pytest --collect-only. Root cause: pytest.ini uses --import-mode=importlib; my test dirs (perf_experiments/ and reduce_accum_mechanism/) lacked __init__.py so pytest fell back to a full-path dotted module name colliding with the real ttnn package import chain. Fixed by adding an empty __init__.py to MY OWN reduce_accum_mechanism/ dir only (not the shared perf_experiments/ parent, matching gateup_in0_share siblings pattern) - collection now succeeds, 30 tests collected.

First on-device run (baseline S=1) HUNG. Triage shows root(0,0), row4(0,4), row8(0,8) still GO; root reader stuck at noc_semaphore_wait_min waiting for data_arrivals=1 i.e. its FIRST child (row1, a leaf) never signals SEM_DATA back, even though row1 itself is not shown as stuck (presumably finished/DONE). row4/row8 writers stuck waiting for SEM_GO invite from root (root never gets there since its stuck on child0). Investigating with a reduced 2-core (root+1 leaf) probe via tt-probe.sh to isolate the reduce-transport bug before re-running the full 10-core sweep.

pack_l1_acc variant FAILED numerically (pcc 0.44-0.71, not a hang/crash) at bfp8_b accumulator format while baseline and dest_acc both PASS. Root cause hypothesis: packer L1-accumulation (pack_reconfig_l1_acc raw toggle) does a linear add at the hardware level and REQUIRES a linear format (fp16_b/bf16), same constraint the real op documents for its own cb_gate_interm/cb_up_interm (Float16_b, packer_l1_acc forces >= fp16_b for partials, op_design.md 4.1). bfp8_b is a shared-exponent block-floating-point format - raw accumulate on it is mathematically invalid. Testing pack_l1_acc with bf16 accumulator dtype next to confirm.

Root cause of hang found via 2-row vs 4-row probes: gru_reader.cpp reduce loop did ONE cb_reserve_back/push_back for the WHOLE stage spanning ALL children, instead of per-child (REDUCE_SLOTS=1 needs reserve/invite/wait/push ONCE PER CHILD since the CB holds exactly one slot with no extra depth). Later children overwrote earlier children data before compute consumed it, and compute later per-child waits had no further push coming -> hang. Fixed by moving cb_reserve_back/push_back inside the per-child loop. 2-row (1 child) masked the bug since num_children=1 makes per-stage and per-child collapse identically. Re-testing 4-row case now.

Bisected the hang via tt-probe --dev: a standalone one-shot program running ONLY the baseline logic (a+b+c, M_EFF=8) succeeds. But looping over all 5 VARIANTS via the real run_op()/create_program_descriptor() on the SAME open device (matching the correctness tests structure) hangs on the very FIRST variant (baseline). Since the real kernel source is ONE big kernel_main() with if-constexpr branches selecting among methods 0-4 by a METHOD compile-time-arg, suspect the OTHER unreached branches raw LLK calls (binary_dest_reuse_tiles_init, silu_tile_init, mul_tiles_init) still get compiled into the SAME translation unit (if-constexpr in a non-template function does not prevent compilation, only dead-code-elimination), and some JIT/LLK static config (e.g. dst-sync context count) may be derived from a whole-file scan of which op kinds appear, independent of which branch executes at runtime -- corrupting the UNPACK<->MATH context handshake for the ACTUALLY-taken baseline path. Fix: split into 5 independent kernel source strings (one per variant, no dead if-constexpr branches) instead of one dispatch kernel. Rewriting program_descriptor_with_inline_kernels.py now.

Fix verified on kgroups=2 (PASS), kgroups=4 (PASS, PCC not computed but diff sane), kgroups=10 full topology (PASS, PCC=0.9995 vs quantized-fp32 reference at tiny emb_t=10). Now running the actual pytest correctness suite at real focus shape (emb_t=224) via scripts/run_safe_pytest.sh.

14/15 correctness cases PASSED at focus shape (emb_t=224,KGROUPS=10) after the reader fix, all PCC~0.9994 (well above 0.975 threshold). Only m_s8_pipelined failed with a DIFFERENT, unrelated error: TT_FATAL program size (86384) too large for kernel config buffer (70656) on TENSIX - i.e. 8-way compile-time-unrolled StageRunner blows the kernel-config binary size limit. Preliminary single-shot ns from the correctness run: baseline=143001, hn_s2_serial=137455, hn_s2_pipelined=136275, hn_s3_pipelined=145887, hn_s6_pipelined=166710, m_s2_pipelined=137360, m_s4_pipelined=149987, hn_pad4_baseline=102099, hn_pad4_s2_pipelined=98421, m_eff4_baseline=76972, m_eff4_hn_s2_pipelined=72581, m_eff4_m_s2_pipelined=75537, m_eff1_baseline=27253, m_eff1_hn_s2_pipelined=26886. Removing m_s8 from further runs (code-size infeasible), running remaining focus/predicate cases + repeats for medians next.

Root cause of pack_l1_acc numeric bug (matched exactly: pcc=1/sqrt(fan_in+1) pattern, i.e. acc=last child overwrite not accumulate): PackTileImpl only honors an explicit per-iteration output index (out_idx=base+i_flat) when out_of_order_output=true, which requires TileOffset::Set or chain-level L1Accumulation!=Disabled; with ReservePolicy::None + chain L1Accumulation left Disabled (my raw-toggle design), out_of_order_output was false, so pack_tile fell back to its own internal sequential counter that resets to 0 every separate eltwise_chain call - each fold call silently overwrote from tile 0 instead of continuing at the prior physical position. Fixed by adding TileOffset::Set{0} to the AccFoldPack output spec in both the main kernel (VARIANT==1) and the fuse-gate-up kernel. pack_reconfig_l1_acc is confirmed (pack.h docstring) to be an independent hardware register from out_of_order_output, so this combination should now correctly accumulate at a fixed explicit address. Re-testing now.

Raw transaction-count sweep (reader-only, no tilize/writer): N=1:452ns N=2:462ns N=4:543ns N=8:659ns N=16:909ns N=24:1116ns N=32:1349ns. Marginal slope N=8->32 is ~26-31 ns/transaction, well BELOW the double_buffer report ~110-125ns/transaction whole-tile-bandwidth floor -- but that floor is a STEADY-STATE THROUGHPUT number over many rounds, while this is a single latency-overlapped burst, so they measure different regimes and are not directly comparable. KEY FINDING: the raw 32-read+barrier cost is only ~1.3us in isolation, far below the real ops reported 15.2us mean/41.5us max on the injector core -- meaning the gap is dominated by MULTI-CORE CONTENTION (110 cores vs 8 DRAM banks) and surrounding-barrier interaction (the W_gate prefetch barrier also drains under this), NOT a raw per-transaction-cost problem in the read pattern itself. This redirects the useful lever toward reducing CONTENTION/overlap, not toward fewer transactions. Proceeding to predicate sweep across kr_pad/emb.

Predicate sweep confirmed consistent ranking across kr_pad in {19,20,22,23} x emb in {6144,7168}: dual_noc_split WIN ~12-13pct uniformly (zero L1 cost); wide_read_individual and bank_run_grouped REGRESSION ~2.3-2.6x uniformly (also need ~448KB extra L1, far beyond ~38KB slack, undeployable regardless of timing); bfp8_tile_direct (existing supported format) bounds RM/tilize overhead at ~46-48pct of baseline; self_copy ablation shows self-copy is ~10-12pct of stage. All correctness gated variants bit-identical to baseline or PCC>=0.999 vs ttnn reference. Finalizing report to coordinator.

Confirmed 2nd hang cause via --dev LLK assert: are_unpackers_AB_configured_correctly failed in fused_up_mul. add_tiles needs dual-operand AB unpack config (add_tiles_init); binary_dest_reuse_tiles needs single-operand A config (binary_dest_reuse_tiles_init). Hoisting both inits ONCE above the m_eff row loop let row0s dest-reuse calls leave the unpacker in single-A mode, silently breaking row1s add_tiles. Fixed by re-issuing both inits every row (2x M_EFF total, still only 8 fused DEST windows for m_eff=8). Re-ran the 5-variant bisection probe (all sequential on one open device, one regime): all 5 now RUNNING+DONE, no hang. Proceeding to full correctness test.

Full correctness test passes: 20/20 combos (5 variants x 4 regimes), PCC 0.99978-0.99982, well above 0.975 threshold and the ops 0.9797 bfp4 format floor (this bench only carries one bfp8 hop, no bfp4 matmuls). Fused variants (fused_up_mul, fused_math_silu) show slightly HIGHER PCC than baseline/blocked_3pass/hoisted_bias (0.99981 vs 0.99979) as predicted -- they skip the extra bfp8 round-trip of up_sum through L1. Proceeding to device-ns perf measurement (test_root_epilogue_fusion_device_perf).

Probed pack_l1_acc with identical random data at bf16 vs bfp8_b (fan_in=4,block_tiles=48): bf16 max_abs_diff=0.0065 (correct, quantization-level noise); bfp8_b max_abs_diff=1.17 (badly wrong). CONFIRMED: the packer raw L1-accumulate hardware register only does a valid linear add for bf16/fp16/fp32 - bfp8_b is a shared-exponent block-floating-point format and a raw hardware accumulate on it is mathematically invalid. This exactly matches the real ops own design note (op_design.md 4.1): packer_l1_acc forces >= fp16_b for partials, and the real op NEVER uses packer_l1_acc on its bfp8_b cb_gate_acc/cb_reduce_*_in CBs, only on the bf16 cb_*_interm CBs. CONCLUSION: pack_l1_acc is only a valid mechanism when PAIRED with the bf16 intermediate-format change (option 4) - it cannot be graduated standalone against the ops current bfp8_b accumulator. Restructuring test/report to measure pack_l1_acc at bf16 and baseline/dest_acc at bfp8_b (current format).

All device-ns sweeps complete, 3 repeats for focus cases (noise ~0.5%), 1 repeat for predicate sweep. Verdict: WIN but modest. Best = HN-axis S=2 pipelined -4.70pct vs baseline at focus shape (136275 vs 143001ns median). M-axis S=2 pipelined close second at -3.88pct. S=3+ is a consistent REGRESSION on both axes, worsening with S, catastrophic at hn_pad=4,S=4 (-41.8pct). Separated DEST-shrink cost (serial-vs-baseline) from overlap gain (pipelined-vs-serial): overlap gain is small and roughly constant (0.3-1.2pct) regardless of S; the S=2 win is mostly driven by breaking the monolithic matmul+reduce cycle into 2 rounds (a schedule effect visible even in serial mode), not by explicit instruction reordering. Per-stage fixed overhead ~6-10us (HN slightly worse than M due to extra DEST/init cost). m_s8_pipelined BLOCKED (program size exceeds kernel config buffer - 8-way compile-time unroll too large). Writing final report to coordinator now.

All 27 correctness cases (3 mechanisms x 3 fan_in x 3 block_tiles) PASS after fixing pack_l1_acc (TileOffset::Set fix + measuring it at its only valid format, bf16). Running the main device-perf sweep next.

Device-ns results (3-trial median, kernel_iters=30, 4 regimes): baseline vs candidates. Focus (48 tiles) baseline=53571ns; blocked_3pass=50812(1.05x); hoisted_bias=50141(1.07x, best); fused_up_mul=51049(1.05x); fused_math_silu=50857(1.05x). Same ordering/magnitude across count128(24t)/count32(6t)/ragged hn_pad4(32t) regimes -- consistent, modest ~4-7% win, NOT the large win the window-count theory predicted. Root cause: tile-op count (144 add/mul/pack calls) is IDENTICAL across all 5 variants regardless of windowing -- the per-tile-op cost (~350ns) dominates over per-window/per-call reconfig overhead, which is only a small fraction. hoisted_bias (block b/c + hoist a reconfig) ties-or-beats the fuller DEST-reuse fusion (fused_up_mul) in every regime, because the fused variant must re-issue BOTH add_tiles_init and binary_dest_reuse_tiles_init every row (discovered via device hang: mixing add_tiles/binary_dest_reuse_tiles with inits hoisted ONCE corrupts the AB-unpacker config, caught by --dev LLK assert are_unpackers_AB_configured_correctly) -- that per-row dual-reinit tax roughly cancels the L1-round-trip savings. fused_math_silu (MATH-thread SiLU, no packer overlap) is within noise of fused_up_mul (packer-thread SiLU) in every regime -- the packer/math overlap trick shows no measurable value at this isolated single-row scale. Verdict: WIN (modest, ~5-7%) for blocked_3pass/hoisted_bias; NULL for going further to full up+mul fusion (no net gain over hoisting alone, though it does drop the up_sum scratch CB, ~52KB L1, which may matter given the op is L1-constrained per Refinement 3). Finalizing report to coordinator.

ROUND-1 HANG ROOT-CAUSED. Not the in-place add. cb_push_back writes the PUSHING RISC-V local tiles_received counter into the shared L1 counter (it OVERWRITES, not increments). Seeding cb_gate_acc from NCRISC and then running the in-place add makes PACK a SECOND pusher of the same CB with its own local counter at 0, so PACKs first push RESETS the shared received count backwards (12 -> 8) and UNPACK cb_wait_front deadlocks on window 2. Triage: root (0,0) ncrisc stuck at reader noc_semaphore_wait_min; row2 (0,2) brisc stuck at cb_wait_front(cb_gate_send) because its compute (1 child = the only core doing an in-place add) hung. INVARIANT: exactly ONE RISC-V may ever cb_push_back a given CB. FIX: reader seeds cb_gate_in/cb_up_in; the first reduce add is OUT-OF-PLACE (gate_in + rg_in -> gate_acc) so the pass count stays byte-identical to the op and PACK is the sole pusher of gate_acc.

CONFIRMED kernel_lib BUG: eltwise_chain produces WRONG VALUES from the SECOND DEST window onward for any chain that mixes a CB-reader FPU element (BinaryFpu/CopyTile, dual-operand AB unpack config) with DestReuseBinary (single-operand A config) — the per-element init is hoisted out of the blocked walk, so after window 1 leaves the unpacker in single-A mode the add_tiles/copy_tile of window 2+ runs under the wrong config. Measured: block_tiles=6 (ONE window) fuse_silu_mul PCC 0.999807 / fuse_up_mul 0.999817 / sigacc_mul 0.999676 (all correct); block_tiles=12 (TWO windows) 0.9815 / 0.9464; block_tiles=48 (six) 0.9723. Same failure round 1 hit with raw LLK (root_epilogue_fusion fused_bc comment). Workaround: one eltwise_chain CALL per DEST window so the setup is re-emitted.

My hoist hypothesis was WRONG. Real mechanism, isolated by sweeping the DEST window width at fixed 48 tiles: an eltwise_chain containing DestReuseBinary is CORRECT at window <=7 and CORRUPT at window 8 (= DEST_AUTO_LIMIT). It needs ONE SPARE DEST slot; chain_max_block_value() (eltwise_chain.inl:1482-1493) only subtracts that slot on the any_dest_accumulation branch, so block_size 8 is admitted and silently overruns. Measured at 48 tiles: fuse_silu_mul PCC 0.999828 at blk 1/2/3/4/5/6/7 vs 0.972295 at blk 8; fuse_up_mul 0.999810 vs 0.912151. AND the corrected precision picture is a WIN: single_pass PCC 0.999946 (0/48 tiles off by >0.05) and fuse_silu_mul 0.999828 both BEAT the shipped baseline 0.999793, because they skip the bfp8 round trip of cb_gate_silu and (single_pass) do the SwiGLU multiply on the SFPU instead of the LoFi FPU.

L1: slots2 = +104448 B (fits 143360 free); slots4 = +313344 (does NOT fit) and is only 0.1% better.

VERDICT WIN. Recommended: dir_noc + REDUCE_SLOTS=2 + PER-SLOT push/counters = add-mode 21201->19642 (-7.35%) at the focus shape, BIT-IDENTICAL, +104448 B L1 (fits).
